answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate is binding, and the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle; memory_c6 says multi-year volume pricing only applies with an incumbent renewal, and that door is closed. memory_c2 is the one inherited record that directly speaks to switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor, and its specifics are exactly what this decision will live or die on: whether last year's sharp unit-cost cut held, whether onboarding truly stayed quick, and whether invoicing stayed accurate. I want that original record before committing, because switching is the only candidate that plausibly meets finance's mandate within 14 days without a second source. Primary objective is minimum total cost of ownership without increasing delivery risk, not minimum unit price, so the low-cost quote alone is not enough: a vendor switch that delays parts to an assembly line already at 94% of committed volume and without buffer would create severe downstream cost. That is why I flag downstream value risk and condition execution on an incoming-delivery proof plan: confirmed lead time, first-article or lot inspection, expedited first shipment if possible, and a short fallback if the first delivery slips. The contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew, so defer_decision is unacceptable; add_second_source takes more time than one cycle and does not by itself meet the 18% mandate; negotiate_terms is blocked by the incumbent's refusal. renew_incumbent avoids delivery risk but fails the cost mandate. Therefore the intended decision is switch_primary_vendor to the low-cost vendor, subject to memory_c2 verification and delivery-risk controls.
